screens.name: Cold launch, first item
screens.purpose: A child who has never opened the app is being taught within fifteen seconds, having read nothing

regions.label: Exit (icon only, top-left, always present)
The grapheme, very large, instructional letterform (single-story a and g)
Speaker button: replays the phoneme. Large, centre, obviously tappable
No title. No welcome. No name field. No age field. No account.
Continue: a forward chevron, icon-only, thumb-height

notes: Replaces the shipped OnboardingView, which opens 'Welcome, Parent!' and collects name and age - a child alone cannot get past it
Phoneme audio autoplays once on entry, then waits. It never loops unprompted
First-run: identical to every later run. There is no first-run variant, deliberately
Offline is the normal state, not an error. Nothing on this screen implies a connection

screens.name: Sound introduction
screens.purpose: Introduce one phoneme and its spelling, replayable without limit

regions.label: Exit  |  progress dots (position only, no percentage, no timer)
Grapheme at display size with the mouth-shape cue beside it
Speaker button, primary. Tapping anywhere else also interrupts audio
Example word, spoken and shown, using only graphemes already taught
Continue (icon-only chevron)

notes: Any tap interrupts narration immediately - this is the incumbent's single loudest complaint
Reduced motion: mouth-shape cue is a static illustration rather than an animation
No text is load-bearing. A child who reads nothing on this screen can still proceed

screens.name: Tracing canvas
screens.purpose: Child traces the grapheme with guided stroke order and forgiving tolerance

regions.label: Exit  |  replay sound  |  progress dots
Trace target: glyph scaled to fit the canvas, stroke-order ghost, start dot
Stroke counter as dots, not numerals
Skip this item (always available, never penalised)

notes: Fixes the shipped defect: makeLetterPath hardcodes 300pt and centres but never scales, so a two-glyph blend renders ~1236pt on a ~350pt canvas
Multi-glyph targets (sh, bl, ai) must fit the same canvas as a single glyph
Tolerance is forgiving by design; motor difficulty frequently co-occurs and is not what we are assessing
Success animation is brief and quiet. No confetti, no fanfare, no score

screens.name: Blending
screens.purpose: Push taught sounds together into a word at a pace the child controls

regions.label: Exit  |  progress dots
Graphemes laid out separately, each individually tappable to hear its sound
Blend control: child drags the sounds together, controlling speed with the gesture
The assembled word, revealed only after the child completes the blend
Continue

notes: New surface. The engine is pure Domain (BlendingEngine) per ADR-000 D9
The child sets the tempo. No automatic blending animation the child has to sit through
Each grapheme remains tappable throughout, so a child can re-hear one sound without restarting

screens.name: Word building, Elkonin boxes
screens.purpose: Child places graphemes into one box per phoneme, making the sound-to-spelling map visible

regions.label: Exit  |  replay word  |  progress dots
Elkonin boxes: one box per phoneme, sized to the grapheme they take
Grapheme tray: draggable tiles including plausible distractors
Spoken word prompt, replayable
Check

notes: New surface. Boxes are the standard multisensory apparatus and must read as boxes, not as a spelling test
A wrong tile returns to the tray without commentary. No red, no buzzer, no shake
Distractors are phonologically plausible, never arbitrary

screens.name: Mastery check
screens.purpose: Confirm a skill is held without the screen reading as a test

regions.label: Exit  |  progress dots
The item, presented identically to ordinary practice
Response options, large targets, icon and audio supported
Continue

notes: Must be visually indistinguishable from practice. A child who knows they are being tested performs worse and this population has been tested constantly
No score, no percentage, no 'quiz' framing, no results summary
Mastery is inferred across items by PacingEngine, never announced on a single answer

screens.name: After a wrong answer
screens.purpose: The highest-stakes screen in the product: recover from an error without implying deficiency

regions.label: Exit  |  progress dots
The same item, with one targeted cue added - not a restatement of the lesson
A single scaffold: the first sound, or one box pre-filled
Try again

notes: The incumbent's defining failure is a remedial lecture triggered by two wrong answers. We add one cue and return control
No error colour, no error sound, no 'not quite', no counter of attempts
After a second miss the item is set aside for spaced review and the session moves on. The child is never stuck

screens.name: Session complete
screens.purpose: End a session on a satisfying, brief, entirely unmonetised note

regions.label: What was learned this session, shown as the graphemes themselves
One short line of specific, earned acknowledgement
Done

notes: No upsell. No paywall. No account prompt. No 'save your progress'. No streak. No next-session countdown
Deletes the shipped behaviour where a paywall auto-presents to the child after three missions
Brief by design - a child who wants to stop should be able to leave in one tap

screens.name: Pause and exit
screens.purpose: Leave from anywhere, in one action, at no cost

regions.label: Sheet: Keep going  |  Leave  |  Parent area (small, low contrast, bottom)
No warning, no confirmation, no progress-loss message

notes: Reachable from every child screen via the persistent top-left control
Progress is saved continuously, so there is genuinely nothing to lose and nothing to warn about
The parent entry point lives here and is deliberately unattractive to a child

screens.name: Parental gate
screens.purpose: Keep a child out of the adult area without administering a reading test

regions.label: Close (returns straight to learning)
Arithmetic challenge rendered as numerals: 13 x 4
Number pad, numerals only
One line explaining this is for a grown-up

notes: Numeric, never the conventional spelled-out-word gate. Dyslexia is strongly heritable, so a reading gate is a literacy test on a parent who may share the diagnosis
A wrong answer regenerates a new problem silently. No lockout, no attempt counter
Required for App Store Kids Category; no gate exists in the shipped app today

screens.name: Parent area
screens.purpose: Tell an adult what this is, what it teaches, what it costs, and what it collects

regions.label: < Back to learning
What this teaches, in plain language, no jargon and no diagnosis claims
Cost: free. All of it. Forever. Stated without qualification
Data: nothing leaves this device. No account, no analytics, no network
Settings: audio volume, reduced motion, reset progress
Research study: join with a code (optional, off by default)

notes: This is the screen a teacher reads before deciding whether to recommend the app
The zero-collection statement must be literally true per ADR-000 D1, not a summary of a policy
Reset progress is destructive and irreversible with no cloud copy - confirm, and say so plainly
No diagnosis language anywhere. We teach; we do not identify dyslexia

screens.name: Research study consent
screens.purpose: The one consented path where anything leaves the device

regions.label: < Back
Exactly what is sent: sessions started, skills reached, days since first open
Exactly what is never sent: name, age, voice, drawings, device id, anything identifying
Study code from the teacher or the study team
Leave the study: one tap, deletes the token, stops all uploads
Join the study

notes: Off by default. ADR-000 D6 - the sole exception to the zero-network rule
Written for a parent, at a reading level that does not assume the parent reads fluently either
Revocation must be as prominent as joining, and take effect immediately

flows.label: second miss: set aside for review, move on
